chapter: Sarah Vaughan and the Basie band
title: Sarah Vaughan, Ella Fitzgerald and Mrs. Vaughan at Hidden Hills
summary: Anecdotes about Sarah before a performance, Ella's admiration for Sarah, and his wife looking after Sarah's mother.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Gee, I'm trying to remember who else was in the group. But Sarah and I, we were in the lobby, and I can always tell by an expression on her face when she's serious about something. And she had her daughter with her. We called her Sass, you know? That's her nickname. And I said, "Well, Sass, now what are you thinking about now?" And she would say, "Jones, I'm just trying to think about what to sing and how I'm going to sing it." I told her, "All you need to do is just get up to the microphone, and it'll come out."
That's the way it works with her.
Yeah. Just get to the microphone and --

I'll tell you an interesting thing. You know, when I was working with Ella Fitzgerald the first time I walked into her living room, there's a big picture of Ella and Sarah together. Ella admires Sarah. There's some mutual admiration society going on there, you know? And a thing I had to promise myself to do, and I never got to it, and I may get to it someday, Sarah Vaughan's mother always wanted to meet Ella. I just never got to it, because I was taking care of some other responsibilities at that time, you know? And Ella's moved now. She's moved -- oh, she's still out in Beverly Hills, and I think she still has the same phone number. But one day I think I'm going to do it, go by and pick her up and take her out to Sarah's house, you know, and let Mrs. Vaughan --
Does Sarah's mother live with her?
Yes. She's out -- well, after her father died she moved out here.
I didn't realize that.
Yeah. A beautiful place, out in Hidden Hills, you know.
Yeah. Saw the big swimming pool that Sarah can't swim in.
Yeah. The kids use it.
Sarah says she's going to take lessons. She's determined to learn. Every day she goes out there and looks at it.
Yeah. No, she might do it.
I know think she loves it out there.

Yeah. It's -- I've stayed out there on weekends, you know. My wife and I used to go out there. And my wife used to take care of Carmen's mother before she passed, and then Sarah realized that her mother was -- while she's on the road, that her mother was out there in Hidden Hills alone, you know.
Uh-huh.
And so Sarah used to ask my wife to go out there and stay with Mrs. Vaughan, you know?
Uh-huh.
So I'd go out and stay overnight myself with them. And there's a studio where I could write and work, so there was no problem.
That's a lovely place.
Yeah. It was no problem, you know?
